items.title: TowerBridge: Bridging the Dual-Encoder Modality Gap via Weight-Space Programming
items.summary_1line: TowerBridge is a closed-form weight-editing recipe for CLIP-style dual encoders that attenuates directions where the image and text towers agree on hard negatives, raising COCO and Flickr30k retrieval across 21 checkpoints.
items.editor_note: Applied weight editing to CLIP-style retrieval with a closed-form recipe, not LLM-authored weights.

items.title: Looped Weight-Space Programming: use AI to set model weights
items.summary_1line: Researchers from MBZUAI report that Claude Opus 5.5 solved only 26% of hard mazes directly, but wrote a transformer by setting its weights directly, which solves 100% of their test mazes in 39 minutes for $19 without training.
items.editor_note: First cost and success figures: a written transformer beat its author model's direct answers.

editorial.tldr: An MIT report that a frontier LLM can write and read small neural network weights in a single reply set off a run of follow-ups in mid-November: an open-source instruction set (W-ISA), a game-agent compilation paper, and an independent replication. A Nov 18 paper then moved from capability edits to value edits, and a Nov 23 CLIP paper borrowed the name for a closed-form weight-editing recipe.
editorial.whats_new: MBZUAI researchers report Claude Opus 5.5 solved only 26% of hard mazes directly, but a transformer it wrote by setting weights solved 100% of their test mazes in 39 minutes for $19, with no training run.
editorial.why_it_matters: If an LLM can hand-author a small model that beats its own direct answers, weight-writing becomes a cheap way to build narrow task solvers, and an untracked way to change a model's behavior.
editorial.take_for_builders: Treat LLM-written weights as a research option for narrow, verifiable tasks only. Add checkpoint hashing and behavior regression evals now, since direct weight edits leave no training trail.

beats.headline: W-ISA proposes an instruction set for programming LLM weights
Papers compile game rules into agents and reproduce the core claim
beats.summary: One paper tests whether compiled game agents generalize to held-out levels; another reproduces the MIT write-weights and read-weights results.

beats.headline: Weight edits aimed at ethical priorities and CLIP retrieval
beats.summary: A value-edit study on a concept-supervised text model and a closed-form CLIP recipe reported across 21 checkpoints; the CLIP work shares the name more than the LLM-authored method.

beats.headline: LLM-written transformer solves all test mazes for $19
beats.summary: Looped weight-space programming beats the same model's direct answers, 100% versus 26% on hard mazes.

open_questions: Does weight-space programming work beyond small networks, on production-scale LLM layers?
Does the MBZUAI maze result hold on tasks other than mazes, and has anyone reproduced it?
Can weight-space edits be detected by inspecting a served checkpoint?
Does W-ISA gain adoption or a reference implementation from a major lab?
